rules.title: Password history size is configured
rules.explanation: This setting specifies how many unique new passwords must be used before an old password can be reused (Enforce password history).
rules.impact: Reusing the same password for a long period increases the risk of compromise through guessing or credential theft. If an account has already been compromised, a reused password remains usable until the password history forces a change to a new value.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy

rules.title: Maximum password age is configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the maximum number of days a password can be used before the system requires the user to change it.
rules.impact: A maximum age that is too short can push users toward insecure workarounds such as writing passwords down. A maximum age that is too long gives an attacker more time to crack a password and, if the account is already compromised, extends the window of misuse.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy

rules.title: Minimum password age is configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the minimum number of days a password must remain in use before a user is allowed to change it again.
rules.impact: Without a minimum password age, users can immediately cycle through enough new passwords to defeat Enforce password history and return to a familiar or previously compromised password.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy

rules.title: Minimum password length is configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the minimum number of characters required for user account passwords.
rules.impact: Short passwords are significantly more vulnerable to brute-force and password-guessing attacks.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy

rules.title: Password complexity requirements are enabled
rules.explanation: This setting requires passwords to meet complexity rules, such as including a mix of character types rather than only letters.
rules.impact: Passwords that use only uppercase or lowercase letters, without digits or special characters, are easier to compromise through brute-force attacks.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy

rules.title: Account lockout duration is configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines how long a locked-out account remains locked before it is automatically unlocked.
rules.impact: Without a defined lockout duration, failed password-guessing attempts are less effectively disrupted, increasing the likelihood of account compromise.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy

rules.title: Account lockout threshold is configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines how many failed logon attempts are allowed before an account is locked out.
rules.impact: Without a lockout threshold, an attacker can attempt unlimited password guesses using automated brute-force tools.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy

rules.title: Reset account lockout counter is configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines how long must elapse after a failed logon before the failed-logon counter is reset to zero.
rules.impact: An attacker may deliberately generate failed logons across many accounts to cause widespread lockouts. A reasonable reset interval balances protection against password guessing with automatic recovery so administrators are not forced to unlock every account manually.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy

rules.title: Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeTrustedCredManAccessPrivilege) determines which accounts can be used by Credential Manager during Backup and Restore.
rules.impact: An account granted this right can create an application that calls Credential Manager and retrieves credentials stored for other users.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Access this computer from the network is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeNetworkLogonRight) determines which users and groups can connect to the computer over the network.
rules.impact: Overly broad network logon rights expand remote attack surface and can enable unauthorized connections or tool-assisted attacks against the system.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Act as part of the operating system is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeTcbPrivilege) allows a process to assume the identity of any user and gain access to the same local resources as that user. It should not be assigned to any account.
rules.impact: Abuse of this privilege enables a process to impersonate any user without authentication and obtain equivalent local access, which can lead to full system compromise.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Adjust memory quotas for a process is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeIncreaseQuotaPrivilege) determines which accounts can change the maximum memory that can be consumed by a process.
rules.impact: Excessive assignment of this right can allow an attacker to exhaust system memory and cause a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Allow log on locally is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeInteractiveLogonRight) determines which users and groups are allowed to log on interactively at the console.
rules.impact: Unrestricted local logon increases the chance that an unauthorized user can gain console access and then introduce malware or escalate privileges.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeRemoteInteractiveLogonRight) determines which users and groups can log on through Remote Desktop Services (RDP).
rules.impact: Unrestricted Remote Desktop logon rights can allow unauthorized users to establish remote interactive sessions and attempt privilege escalation or malware execution.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Back up files and directories is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeBackupPrivilege) determines which users can circumvent file and directory permissions for the purpose of backing up the system.
rules.impact: Users who can back up data can move backup media to another system where they have administrative rights, restore the data, take ownership of files, and view any unencrypted content in the backup set.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Change the system time is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeSystemtimePrivilege) determines which users can change the date and time on the computer's internal clock.
rules.impact: Changing system time can falsify event-log and file timestamps and disrupt Kerberos authentication, which requires clocks to stay within the allowed skew. Combined with stopping or misconfiguring Windows Time, this can seriously impair authentication and incident investigation.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Change the time zone is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeTimeZonePrivilege) determines which users can change the time zone used by the computer.
rules.impact: Changing the time zone alters how event timestamps are presented and can complicate correlation and forensic analysis during an incident.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Create a pagefile is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeCreatePagefilePrivilege) determines which users can create and change the size of a paging file.
rules.impact: An attacker could shrink the paging file excessively or place it on a fragmented volume, degrading system performance or contributing to a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Create a token object is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeCreateTokenPrivilege) allows a process to create an access token. It should not be assigned to any account.
rules.impact: Accounts that can create or modify tokens can change the effective access level of authenticated accounts, elevate privileges, or contribute to a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Create global objects is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeCreateGlobalPrivilege) determines which users can create global objects that are available to all sessions.
rules.impact: Creating global objects can interfere with processes in other user sessions and lead to application failures or data corruption.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment
rules.default: Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE

rules.title: Create permanent shared objects is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeCreatePermanentPrivilege) determines which accounts can create permanent shared objects in the Windows object manager namespace. It should not be assigned to any account.
rules.impact: Abuse of this right can interfere with shared kernel objects used across sessions and contribute to application failures, data corruption, or denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Create symbolic links is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege) determines which users can create symbolic links on the file system.
rules.impact: Users who can create symbolic links may expose the system to symlink-based attacks that alter effective permissions, corrupt or destroy data, or cause a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Debug programs is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeDebugPrivilege) determines which users can attach a debugger to any process or to the kernel.
rules.impact: Debug rights provide deep access to sensitive operating-system components and process memory. Broad assignment significantly increases the risk of credential theft and privilege escalation.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Deny access to this computer from the network is configured
rules.explanation: This user right (SeDenyNetworkLogonRight) denies network logon for specified accounts. Guests, local accounts, and anonymous logons should be denied (applicable to member servers that are not domain controllers).
rules.impact: Failing to deny network logon for high-risk identities expands remote attack surface and can enable unauthorized connections or tool-assisted attacks.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Deny log on as a batch job is configured
rules.explanation: This user right (SeDenyBatchLogonRight) denies batch logon for specified accounts. Members of the Guests group should be denied.
rules.impact: Batch logon can be abused to schedule jobs that consume excessive resources and contribute to a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Deny log on as a service is configured
rules.explanation: This user right (SeDenyServiceLogonRight) determines which accounts cannot register a process as a service. When an account is subject to both policies, this deny right supersedes Log on as a service.
rules.impact: Accounts that can log on as a service can be used to install and start unauthorized services, including malware. The protective value is limited if an attacker already has administrative rights, but denying the right still reduces misuse of lower-privileged accounts.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Deny log on locally is configured
rules.explanation: This user right (SeDenyInteractiveLogonRight) denies interactive console logon for specified accounts. Members of the Guests group should be denied.
rules.impact: Unauthorized local logon can enable malware execution, privilege escalation, and other attacks that exploit physical or console access.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeEnableDelegationPrivilege) allows users to change the Trusted for Delegation setting on computer and user accounts in Active Directory. It should not be assigned on member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Abuse of unconstrained delegation trust can allow unauthorized users to act on behalf of other network users and escalate access across the domain.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Force shutdown from a remote system is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeRemoteShutdownPrivilege) determines which users can shut down a computer from a remote location on the network.
rules.impact: A user with remote shutdown rights can force the system offline and cause a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Generate security audits is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeAuditPrivilege) determines which accounts can add entries to the security log. It is typically limited to Local Service and Network Service.
rules.impact: An attacker who can generate large volumes of audit events can obscure malicious activity. If the security log overwrites as needed, evidence of unauthorized activity may be lost.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Impersonate a client after authentication is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeImpersonatePrivilege) determines which accounts can impersonate a client after authentication.
rules.impact: Without restricting this right, an unauthorized user could impersonate a client, connect to a service they control, and escalate privileges toward administrative or SYSTEM level.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment
rules.default: Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE

rules.title: Increase scheduling priority is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeIncreaseBasePriorityPrivilege) determines which users can increase the base priority class of a process.
rules.impact: Raising a process to real-time priority can starve other processes of CPU time and result in a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Load and unload device drivers is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeLoadDriverPrivilege) determines which users can dynamically load and unload device drivers. This requirement applies to member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Loading untrusted or malicious drivers can compromise kernel integrity, destabilize the system, or install persistent malware with elevated privileges.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Lock pages in memory is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) allows a process to keep data in physical memory so it is never paged to disk. It should not be assigned to any account.
rules.impact: Abuse of this right can pin large amounts of physical memory and substantially degrade system performance.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Log on as a batch job is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeBatchLogonRight) allows accounts to log on using the Task Scheduler service and other batch-logon mechanisms.
rules.impact: Broad assignment of Log on as a batch job can be abused to run scheduled tasks that consume resources or execute malicious code after an attacker obtains a lower-privileged foothold.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Manage auditing and security log is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeSecurityPrivilege) determines which users can specify object access auditing options and manage the security event log.
rules.impact: Accounts that can change auditing settings or clear the security log can conceal malicious activity and delay detection.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Modify an object label is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeRelabelPrivilege) determines which accounts can modify the integrity label of objects owned by other users. It should not be assigned to any account.
rules.impact: Changing another user's object integrity label can cause code to run at a higher integrity level than intended and enable privilege escalation.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Modify firmware environment values is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeSystemEnvironmentPrivilege) determines which users can modify firmware environment values that affect hardware configuration.
rules.impact: Anyone with this right can alter firmware environment settings in ways that disable hardware components or cause a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Perform volume maintenance tasks is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeManageVolumePrivilege) determines which users can run privileged maintenance tasks on disk volumes, such as defragmentation and remote volume management.
rules.impact: Abuse of volume maintenance rights can allow deletion or reconfiguration of volumes, causing data loss or a denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Profile single process is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeProfileSingleProcessPrivilege) determines which users can use performance-monitoring tools to observe the performance of non-system processes.
rules.impact: An attacker can abuse this right to identify critical processes, security software, and logged-on users, then target those processes or avoid protective controls.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Replace a process level token is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege) determines which accounts can replace the access token associated with a child process that is started by another process.
rules.impact: Users with Replace a process level token can start processes as another user when they know that user's credentials, enabling privilege escalation and lateral movement.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Restore files and directories is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeRestorePrivilege) determines which users can bypass file, directory, registry, and other object permissions when restoring backed-up data. This requirement applies to member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: An attacker with restore rights can overwrite legitimate data or executables with malicious versions, causing data loss, corruption, privilege escalation, or persistent backdoor access.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Shut down the system is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeShutdownPrivilege) determines which users who are logged on locally can shut down the operating system.
rules.impact: Unrestricted shutdown rights can take servers offline, disrupt authentication and directory services on domain controllers, and interrupt workloads that do not otherwise grant users console administrative access.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment
rules.default: Administrators, Backup Operators,Server Operators, Print Operators

rules.title: Take ownership of files or other objects is restricted
rules.explanation: This user right (SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege) determines which users can take ownership of any securable object, including Active Directory objects, NTFS files and folders, printers, registry keys, services, processes, and threads.
rules.impact: Users with Take ownership of files or other objects can assume control of any object regardless of its ACL and then modify it, which can lead to data disclosure, corruption, or denial of service.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment

rules.title: Administrator account status is disabled
rules.explanation: Accounts: Administrator account status determines whether the built-in local Administrator account is enabled or disabled. This requirement applies to member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: The built-in Administrator account cannot be locked out after failed logons and has a well-known SID, making it a preferred target for brute-force attacks even if the account is renamed.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Accounts: Administrator account status

rules.title: Microsoft accounts are blocked
rules.explanation: Accounts: Block Microsoft accounts (NoConnectedUser) controls whether users can add or sign in with Microsoft accounts for SSO to Microsoft services and other applications.
rules.impact: Microsoft accounts can extend authentication and data access outside organizational control. When they are used, auditing and forensic investigation of account activity are typically more difficult.

rules.title: Guest account status is disabled
rules.explanation: Accounts: Guest account status determines whether the built-in Guest account is enabled. When enabled, unauthenticated network users may access resources available to Guest, Guests, or Everyone. This requirement applies to member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: An enabled Guest account can allow anonymous network access to shared resources and result in data disclosure or tampering.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Accounts: Guest account status

rules.title: Blank passwords are limited to console logon only
rules.explanation: Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only (LimitBlankPasswordUse) prevents remote interactive and network logons for local accounts that have blank passwords.
rules.impact: Blank passwords are a severe security risk. Local accounts created outside domain password policy can retain blank passwords and remain usable for remote access unless this control is enabled.

rules.title: Administrator account is renamed
rules.explanation: Accounts: Rename administrator account changes the name of the built-in Administrator account so it does not use the well-known Administrator name. This requirement applies to member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: The default Administrator account name is widely known, and the account cannot be locked out after failed password attempts, making it an attractive brute-force target.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Accounts: Rename administrator account

rules.title: Guest account is renamed
rules.explanation: Accounts: Rename guest account changes the name of the built-in Guest account so it does not use the well-known Guest name. This requirement applies to member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Renaming the Guest account reduces the likelihood that an attacker can easily identify and target that well-known account name.
rules.scope: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Accounts: Rename guest account

rules.title: Audit: Shut down system immediately if unable to log security audits is disabled
rules.explanation: CrashOnAuditFail controls whether Windows shuts down if it cannot record security events. Enabling this option is associated with certain TCSEC C2 and Common Criteria evaluation requirements.
rules.impact: Forcing an immediate shutdown when the security log cannot be written can create an availability outage that an attacker may trigger by filling the audit subsystem. Keeping this setting disabled avoids that denial-of-service condition on typical production servers.

rules.title: Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media is restricted
rules.explanation: AllocateDASD determines who is allowed to format and eject removable NTFS media.
rules.impact: Users who can remove and take media elsewhere may bypass local access controls, take ownership of files, and view or modify sensitive data on another system.

rules.title: Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers is enabled
rules.explanation: AddPrinterDrivers determines whether users other than administrators can install a printer driver when adding a network printer.
rules.impact: Allowing non-administrators to install printer drivers on servers can reduce stability. An attacker could also install a malicious driver disguised as a printer driver.

rules.title: Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always) is enabled
rules.explanation: RequireSignOrSeal requires that all secure channel traffic initiated by a domain member be signed or encrypted. Logon data sent over the secure channel is always encrypted.
rules.impact: Without always requiring signing or encryption, secure channel traffic may lack integrity protection and leave some data unencrypted, increasing the risk of tampering or interception between the member and domain controller.

rules.title: Domain member: Digitally encrypt secure channel data (when possible) is enabled
rules.explanation: SealSecureChannel configures a domain member to attempt negotiation of encryption for all secure channel traffic it initiates.
rules.impact: Encrypting secure channel data when possible reduces exposure of authentication traffic between the workstation and domain controller. Without encryption negotiation, an attacker on the network path has a greater opportunity to intercept sensitive data.

rules.title: Domain member: Disable machine account password changes is disabled
rules.explanation: DisablePasswordChange controls whether a domain member is allowed to periodically change its computer account password.
rules.impact: Preventing regular machine account password changes leaves computer account credentials static for longer, increasing the window for compromise and misuse.

rules.title: Domain member: Maximum machine account password age is configured
rules.explanation: MaximumPasswordAge defines the maximum age, in days, of a machine account password before the domain member attempts to change it.
rules.impact: Domain members typically change machine passwords about every 30 days. A much longer interval, or a value of 0 that disables changes, gives an attacker more time to crack one or more computer account passwords.

rules.title: Domain member: Require strong (Windows 2000 or later) session key is enabled
rules.explanation: RequireStrongKey requires that a 128-bit session key be used for encrypted secure channel data between a domain member and a domain controller.
rules.impact: Weaker session keys make secure channel traffic easier to attack and can expose authentication material exchanged with the domain controller.

rules.title: Interactive logon: Do not display last user name is enabled
rules.explanation: DontDisplayLastUserName determines whether the account name of the last interactive user is displayed on the logon screen.
rules.impact: Displaying the last logged-on user name helps an attacker with console access identify valid accounts and focus password-guessing or other attacks.

rules.title: Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL is disabled
rules.explanation: DisableCAD determines whether users must press CTRL+ALT+DEL before logging on. When this setting is disabled, the secure attention sequence is required.
rules.impact: Without requiring CTRL+ALT+DEL, malware can present a fake logon dialog and capture credentials, then reuse them at the user's privilege level.

rules.title: Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit is configured
rules.explanation: InactivityTimeoutSecs defines how many seconds of user inactivity elapse before the interactive session is locked.
rules.impact: Without an inactivity lock, an unattended session can be used by anyone with physical or console access to the workstation or server.

rules.title: Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache is limited
rules.explanation: CachedLogonsCount specifies how many unique users' logon information can be cached locally for use when a domain controller is unavailable.
rules.impact: Cached logon credentials stored on the local system can be targeted by an attacker with filesystem access. Limiting the cache size reduces the number of credential sets retained on the host.

rules.title: Interactive logon: Prompt user to change password before expiration is configured
rules.explanation: PasswordExpiryWarning defines how many days in advance users are warned that their password will expire.
rules.impact: Without advance warning, users may be locked out when passwords expire, disrupting local and remote access including VPN connections.

rules.title: Interactive logon: Smart card removal behavior is configured
rules.explanation: ScRemoveOption defines the action taken when a smart card used for interactive logon is removed, such as locking the workstation or forcing logoff.
rules.impact: If smart card removal does not lock or log off the session, an unattended authenticated desktop can remain available after the card is removed.

rules.title: Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) is enabled
rules.explanation: RequireSecuritySignature on the SMB client (LanmanWorkstation) requires that the client always digitally sign SMB communications.
rules.impact: Unsigned SMB packets can be intercepted and modified in transit, enabling session hijacking or man-in-the-middle attacks against file and resource sharing traffic.

rules.title: Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (if server agrees) is enabled
rules.explanation: EnableSecuritySignature on the SMB client causes the client to negotiate SMB packet signing when the server supports it.
rules.impact: Negotiating SMB signing when possible reduces the risk of intercepted or modified SMB traffic between the client and servers that support signing.

rules.title: Microsoft network client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers is disabled
rules.explanation: EnablePlainTextPassword determines whether the SMB redirector may send plaintext passwords to third-party SMB servers that do not support password encryption.
rules.impact: Sending unencrypted passwords over the network exposes credentials to interception, especially when connecting to servers that do not implement SMB security mechanisms.

rules.title: Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always) is enabled
rules.explanation: RequireSecuritySignature on the SMB server (LanManServer) requires that the server always digitally sign SMB communications.
rules.impact: Without mandatory SMB signing on the server, attackers on the same network can intercept or modify unsigned SMB sessions and perform unintended actions or gain unauthorized access to shared data.

rules.title: Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (if client agrees) is enabled
rules.explanation: EnableSecuritySignature on the SMB server causes the server to negotiate SMB packet signing with clients that request it.
rules.impact: Negotiating SMB signing with capable clients reduces the risk of session hijacking and man-in-the-middle modification of SMB traffic.

rules.title: Microsoft network server: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire is enabled
rules.explanation: enableforcedlogoff configures the SMB server to forcibly disconnect client sessions when the client's logon hours expire.
rules.impact: Without forced disconnect, users can continue using network resources outside allowed logon hours through sessions established earlier during permitted times.

rules.title: SMB server SPN target name validation level
rules.explanation: This setting controls how the SMB server validates the service principal name (SPN) supplied by a client when establishing an SMB session to shared folders or printers.
rules.impact: SPN validation reduces exposure to SMB relay and related spoofing attacks by confirming the client targets an intended server identity. The setting applies to SMB1 and SMB2.

rules.title: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts
rules.explanation: This Network access policy controls whether anonymous users can enumerate local Security Accounts Manager (SAM) account names on the system.
rules.impact: Anonymous SAM enumeration can reveal account names that adversaries use for password guessing and social engineering. Restricting it reduces reconnaissance opportunities without relying on authenticated access.

rules.title: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares
rules.explanation: This Network access policy controls whether anonymous users can enumerate SAM accounts and share names on the system.
rules.impact: Combined account and share enumeration helps attackers map local users and exposed shares for password guessing, social engineering, or lateral movement. Restricting anonymous enumeration limits that reconnaissance.

rules.title: Do not let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users
rules.explanation: This Network access policy determines whether permissions granted to the Everyone group also apply to anonymous users.
rules.impact: When anonymous users inherit Everyone permissions, they may gain unintended read or other access to resources. Keeping anonymous identities outside Everyone reduces unauthorized access and reconnaissance risk.

rules.title: Named pipes that can be accessed anonymously
rules.explanation: This Network access policy lists named pipes that accept anonymous (null session) connections. On domain controllers, legacy pipes such as COMNAP and LOCATOR historically allowed anonymous access for compatibility.
rules.impact: Unnecessary anonymous named-pipe access expands the network attack surface and can enable unauthorized discovery or use of services. Maintaining a minimal, justified list reduces that exposure.

rules.title: Restrict anonymous access to named pipes and shares
rules.explanation: This Network access policy restricts anonymous (null session) access to named pipes and shares except those explicitly allowed by related Network access settings.
rules.impact: Unrestricted null sessions are a weak access path that can be abused against shares, including default administrative shares. Restricting them limits anonymous reconnaissance and data exposure.

rules.title: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM
rules.explanation: This Network access policy defines which security principals may make remote SAMRPC calls to enumerate local users and groups in the Security Accounts Manager database.
rules.impact: By default, low-privileged network clients can query SAM remotely and obtain reconnaissance useful for further compromise. Restricting remote SAM callers reduces that information disclosure.

rules.title: Shares that can be accessed anonymously
rules.explanation: This Network access policy lists shared folders that anonymous users may access through null sessions.
rules.impact: Anonymous share access can expose or alter sensitive data for any network client that reaches the share. Keeping the list empty or tightly controlled reduces unauthorized disclosure and tampering.

rules.title: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM
rules.explanation: This Network security policy determines whether Local System services that negotiate authentication and fall back to NTLM may use the computer identity instead of a null session.
rules.impact: When Local System falls back to a null session, signing and encryption protections are weaker or absent. Using the computer identity enables stronger session security for NTLM connections where supported.

rules.title: Do not allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback
rules.explanation: This Network security policy controls whether Local System services may fall back to NTLM null sessions when negotiating authentication.
rules.impact: Null-session fallback can produce a system-generated session key that does not meaningfully protect traffic, even when applications attempt to sign or encrypt data. Disallowing the fallback reduces exposure of session data.

rules.title: Do not allow PKU2U authentication requests to use online identities
rules.explanation: This Network security policy controls whether PKU2U authentication requests to this computer may use online identities, such as a Microsoft account.
rules.impact: Allowing online identities can associate a local or peer account with a network identity and enable sign-in without a domain or local Windows account. In domain-joined environments, that path can bypass established authentication controls.

rules.title: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos
rules.explanation: This Network security policy specifies which Kerberos encryption types the system may use. Types that are not selected are not permitted. Multiple encryption types may be enabled.
rules.impact: Stronger Kerberos encryption types reduce the risk of ticket and credential compromise. Disabling weaker types can affect compatibility with older clients, services, or applications that do not support modern algorithms.

rules.title: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change
rules.explanation: This Network security policy determines whether a new LAN Manager (LM) hash is stored in the local SAM when a user changes their password.
rules.impact: LM hashes are significantly weaker than NTLM hashes and are easier to crack if the SAM is obtained. Preventing LM hash storage reduces credential theft risk after subsequent password changes.

rules.title: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire
rules.explanation: This Microsoft network server policy determines whether SMB clients remain connected after the user account's allowed logon hours expire.
rules.impact: Without forced disconnect, users may keep active sessions outside permitted logon hours and continue accessing resources. Enforcing disconnect upholds logon-hour restrictions on network connections.

rules.title: LAN Manager authentication level
rules.explanation: This Network security policy selects which challenge/response authentication protocols may be used for network logons, including LM, NTLM, and NTLMv2.
rules.impact: Weaker LM and NTLM responses are more susceptible to interception and cracking. Requiring NTLMv2 responses strengthens network authentication and reduces reliance on obsolete LM negotiation.

rules.title: LDAP client signing requirements
rules.explanation: This Network security policy sets the LDAP data signing level requested by client devices when issuing LDAP bind requests.
rules.impact: Unsigned LDAP traffic is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle modification between client and directory server. Requiring signing makes it harder for an attacker to alter LDAP queries or responses in transit.

rules.title: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP-based clients
rules.explanation: This Network security policy defines the minimum session security that NTLM Security Support Provider (NTLM SSP) clients must negotiate, such as NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption. Effective strength also depends on the LAN Manager authentication level.
rules.impact: NTLM SSP traffic without strong session security can be intercepted or altered by an attacker with network access. Requiring stronger client session security reduces man-in-the-middle exposure.

rules.title: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects
rules.explanation: This System objects policy strengthens the default discretionary access control list (DACL) on internal system objects, such as symbolic links.
rules.impact: A more restrictive default DACL limits non-administrative users to read access on shared objects and prevents them from modifying objects created by other users. That reduces unintended privilege abuse against system objects.

rules.title: Admin Approval Mode for the built-in Administrator account
rules.explanation: This User Account Control (UAC) policy determines whether the built-in Administrator account runs in Admin Approval Mode.
rules.impact: Without Admin Approval Mode, the built-in Administrator account runs with full elevation by default, increasing the risk that malware executes with elevated rights unnoticed. Enabling the mode subjects that account to UAC elevation controls.

rules.title: Elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode
rules.explanation: This User Account Control policy defines how administrators in Admin Approval Mode are prompted for elevation. The recommended baseline behavior is to prompt for consent on the secure desktop.
rules.impact: If elevation occurs without a clear consent prompt, malware may obtain elevated privileges without administrator awareness. Consent on the secure desktop reduces spoofing of the elevation dialog and unauthorized privilege elevation.

rules.title: Elevation prompt for standard users
rules.explanation: This User Account Control policy defines how standard users are handled when an application requests elevation.
rules.impact: Allowing standard users to elevate freely can lead to unintended privilege grants and malware execution with higher rights. A restrictive prompt behavior limits unauthorized elevation attempts.

rules.title: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation
rules.explanation: This User Account Control policy controls whether Windows detects application installer behavior and prompts for elevation before installation proceeds.
rules.impact: Some malware installs components after a trusted application starts. Installation detection provides an additional elevation prompt that can interrupt unauthorized software before it modifies the system.

rules.title: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode
rules.explanation: This User Account Control policy enables Admin Approval Mode for administrator accounts and is the master switch for UAC-related policies on the system.
rules.impact: When this setting is disabled, UAC is effectively turned off and elevation protections that depend on it are not applied. Keeping Admin Approval Mode enabled preserves UAC's privilege-separation benefits.

rules.title: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation
rules.explanation: This User Account Control policy determines whether elevation prompts are displayed on the secure desktop rather than the interactive user desktop.
rules.impact: Elevation dialogs on the interactive desktop can be spoofed by malware to capture credentials or consent. Using the secure desktop reduces that spoofing risk.

rules.title: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations
rules.explanation: This User Account Control policy redirects failed file and registry write attempts by applications into per-user virtualized locations when writes to protected system locations are denied.
rules.impact: Virtualization reduces the need for applications to run elevated solely to write application data, limiting system-wide changes. Constraining writes to permitted locations lowers the impact of poorly behaved or untrusted software.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Domain profile enabled
rules.explanation: This setting enables Windows Defender Firewall for the Domain profile, which applies when the computer is connected to a network identified as a domain network.
rules.impact: A disabled or unconfigured firewall increases the likelihood that remote attackers can reach vulnerable network services. Keeping the Domain profile firewall enabled provides baseline host-based network filtering.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Domain profile default outbound action
rules.explanation: This setting defines the default action Windows Defender Firewall takes for outbound connections in the Domain profile when no explicit rule matches.
rules.impact: Without a controlled default outbound action, unwanted or malicious egress traffic may leave the host more easily. A defined baseline action supports consistent filtering of outbound connections on domain networks.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Domain profile notifications disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows Defender Firewall notifies the interactive user when a connection is blocked under the Domain profile.
rules.impact: Frequent or unclear firewall notifications can confuse users and encourage unsafe local rule changes. Suppressing Domain profile notifications supports centrally managed firewall policy with less end-user interference.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Domain profile log file path
rules.explanation: This setting specifies the path and file name used for Windows Defender Firewall Domain profile logging.
rules.impact: Without a defined firewall log location, dropped and successful connection events may not be retained for review. Logging supports detection and investigation of suspicious network activity on the host.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Domain profile log file size
rules.explanation: This setting configures the maximum size of the Windows Defender Firewall Domain profile log file. A common baseline minimum is 16,384 KB.
rules.impact: An undersized log rolls over quickly and may omit evidence needed during incident response. Adequate log size improves retention of firewall events for investigation and near-real-time detection.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Domain profile log dropped packets
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of dropped packets (DROP events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Domain profile.
rules.impact: Dropped-packet records help reconstruct blocked connection attempts during security investigations. Without them, analysis of denied traffic on domain networks is incomplete.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Domain profile log successful connections
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of successful connections (ALLOW events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Domain profile.
rules.impact: Successful-connection records provide context for permitted traffic during investigations. Including ALLOW events alongside DROP events improves completeness of host firewall telemetry.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile enabled
rules.explanation: This setting enables Windows Defender Firewall for the Private profile, which applies on networks identified as private.
rules.impact: A disabled Private profile firewall leaves local network services more exposed to attackers on trusted or misclassified networks. Enabling it maintains host-based filtering outside domain environments.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile default inbound action
rules.explanation: This setting defines the default action Windows Defender Firewall takes for inbound connections in the Private profile when no explicit rule matches.
rules.impact: An unrestricted default inbound action increases exposure of local services on private networks. A deny-oriented baseline reduces unsolicited remote access risk.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile default outbound action
rules.explanation: This setting defines the default action Windows Defender Firewall takes for outbound connections in the Private profile when no explicit rule matches.
rules.impact: Without a controlled default outbound action, unwanted or malicious egress traffic may leave the host more easily. A defined baseline supports consistent outbound filtering on private networks.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile notifications disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows Defender Firewall notifies the interactive user when a connection is blocked under the Private profile.
rules.impact: Unclear or frequent notifications can distract users and lead to insecure local exceptions. Disabling Private profile notifications supports managed firewall policy with less end-user disruption.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile log file path
rules.explanation: This setting specifies the path and file name used for Windows Defender Firewall Private profile logging.
rules.impact: Without a defined log path, Private profile firewall events may not be available for review. Logging supports detection and investigation of suspicious network activity.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile log file size
rules.explanation: This setting configures the maximum size of the Windows Defender Firewall Private profile log file. A common baseline minimum is 16,384 KB.
rules.impact: An undersized log rolls over quickly and may omit evidence needed during incident response. Adequate log size improves retention of Private profile firewall events.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile log dropped packets
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of dropped packets (DROP events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Private profile.
rules.impact: Dropped-packet records help reconstruct blocked connection attempts during investigations. Without them, analysis of denied traffic on private networks is incomplete.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Private profile log successful connections
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of successful connections (ALLOW events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Private profile.
rules.impact: Successful-connection records provide context for permitted traffic during investigations. Including ALLOW events improves completeness of Private profile firewall telemetry.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile enabled
rules.explanation: This setting enables Windows Defender Firewall for the Public profile, which applies on networks identified as public.
rules.impact: Public networks present higher untrusted-peer risk. A disabled Public profile firewall increases exposure of local services to remote exploitation.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile default inbound action
rules.explanation: This setting defines the default action Windows Defender Firewall takes for inbound connections in the Public profile when no explicit rule matches.
rules.impact: An unrestricted default inbound action on public networks significantly increases remote attack surface. A restrictive baseline reduces unsolicited inbound access risk.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile default outbound action
rules.explanation: This setting defines the default action Windows Defender Firewall takes for outbound connections in the Public profile when no explicit rule matches.
rules.impact: Without a controlled default outbound action, unwanted or malicious egress traffic may leave the host more easily on untrusted networks. A defined baseline supports consistent outbound filtering.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile notifications disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows Defender Firewall notifies the interactive user when a connection is blocked under the Public profile.
rules.impact: Notifications can confuse users and encourage insecure local exceptions on public networks. Disabling them supports centrally managed Public profile firewall policy.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile local rule merge disabled
rules.explanation: This setting determines whether local administrators can create, modify, or merge local Windows Defender Firewall rules with applied Group Policy for the Public profile (AllowLocalPolicyMerge).
rules.impact: Locally created Public profile rules can weaken centrally enforced protections and expose the system. Disabling local rule merge helps keep public-network firewall policy under administrative control.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile local IPsec rule merge disabled
rules.explanation: This setting determines whether local administrators can create, modify, or merge local connection security (IPsec) rules with applied Group Policy for the Public profile (AllowLocalIPsecPolicyMerge).
rules.impact: Local IPsec or connection security exceptions can bypass intended Public profile protections. Disabling local IPsec rule merge preserves centrally managed connection security policy.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile log file path
rules.explanation: This setting specifies the path and file name used for Windows Defender Firewall Public profile logging.
rules.impact: Without a defined log path, Public profile firewall events may not be available for review. Logging supports detection and investigation of suspicious activity on untrusted networks.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile log file size
rules.explanation: This setting configures the maximum size of the Windows Defender Firewall Public profile log file. A common baseline minimum is 16,384 KB.
rules.impact: An undersized log rolls over quickly and may omit evidence needed during incident response. Adequate log size improves retention of Public profile firewall events.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile log dropped packets
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of dropped packets (DROP events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Public profile.
rules.impact: Dropped-packet records help reconstruct blocked connection attempts during investigations. Without them, analysis of denied traffic on public networks is incomplete.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile log successful connections
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of successful connections (ALLOW events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Public profile.
rules.impact: Successful-connection records provide context for permitted traffic during investigations. Including ALLOW events improves completeness of Public profile firewall telemetry.

rules.title: Audit account management
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events related to account management activities, including creation, modification, and deletion of accounts where applicable to the selected subcategory scope.
rules.impact: Account management audit records support detection and investigation of unauthorized privilege changes and account lifecycle abuse on the system.

rules.title: Audit application group management
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when application groups are created, modified, or deleted.
rules.impact: Application group changes can alter access to application resources. Auditing those events aids detection and investigation of unauthorized group management activity.

rules.title: Audit security group management
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when security groups are created, changed, or deleted.
rules.impact: Security group membership changes often grant or remove privileged access. Auditing these events helps identify and investigate unauthorized privilege escalation.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit user account management
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events related to user account management, such as creation, modification, enablement, disablement, or deletion of user accounts.
rules.impact: User account changes are a common path for persistence and privilege abuse. Auditing these events supports detection and investigation of unauthorized account activity.

rules.title: Audit process creation
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when a process is created.
rules.impact: Process creation audit data provides timing and user context for executed programs, which is essential when reconstructing attacker activity during incident response.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit account lockout
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when a user account is locked out after failed logon attempts.
rules.impact: Account lockout events can indicate password-guessing activity or help correlate authentication failures during security investigations.

rules.title: Audit group membership
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records group membership information included in a user's logon token.
rules.impact: Group membership at logon clarifies which privileges were available during a session. That context is valuable when investigating security incidents involving elevated or unexpected access.

rules.title: Audit logoff
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when a user logs off from the system.
rules.impact: Logoff events help establish when a user session ended and support correlation with other security events during incident investigations.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit logon
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when a user attempts to log on to the system.
rules.impact: Logon events establish when sessions begin and are fundamental for reconstructing user activity and correlating authentication with other security events during investigations.

rules.title: Audit other logon/logoff events
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records additional logon and logoff related events beyond the primary Logon and Logoff subcategories, such as Terminal Services session disconnects and reconnects where applicable.
rules.impact: Other logon/logoff events provide session lifecycle detail that complements standard logon and logoff auditing during security investigations.

rules.title: Audit special logon
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records special logon events, including use of elevated or sensitive privileges during logon.
rules.impact: Special logon records highlight privileged session starts. That telemetry is useful when investigating misuse of elevated credentials.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit removable storage
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records successful and failed attempts to access removable storage devices.
rules.impact: Removable media is a common path for data exfiltration and malware introduction. Auditing its use supports detection and investigation of related security incidents.

rules.title: Audit audit policy change
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records changes to audit policy settings on the system.
rules.impact: An attacker with administrative rights may disable or alter auditing to hide further activity. Recording audit policy changes helps detect that concealment technique.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit authentication policy change
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records changes to authentication policy settings.
rules.impact: Authentication policy changes can weaken logon controls or enable new trust paths. Auditing those changes helps detect and investigate tampering that may conceal or enable compromise.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit authorization policy change
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records changes to authorization policy settings that affect access decisions.
rules.impact: Authorization policy changes can expand or remove access rights unexpectedly. Auditing them helps detect privilege manipulation intended to hide or enable further compromise.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit sensitive privilege use
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records when user rights that affect sensitive operations are used.
rules.impact: Sensitive privilege use often accompanies administrative abuse or advanced attacks. Auditing these events supports detection and investigation of privileged activity.

rules.title: Audit IPsec driver
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records system events related to the IPsec driver.
rules.impact: IPsec driver events provide visibility into connection security failures and related system conditions useful during security incident investigation.

rules.title: Audit other system events
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records other system events that are not covered by more specific system audit subcategories, including certain Windows Firewall and cryptographic service events where applicable.
rules.impact: Other system event records fill gaps in host telemetry and support broader investigation of security-relevant system activity.

rules.title: Audit security state change
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when the security state of the system changes, such as system startup and shutdown related security events.
rules.impact: Security state change events establish timeline markers for system availability and security subsystem transitions during incident investigations.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: Audit security system extension
rules.explanation: This advanced audit policy subcategory records events when security system extensions are loaded, such as authentication packages, security packages, or notification packages.
rules.impact: Loading unauthorized security extensions can persist malware or alter authentication behavior. Auditing these events supports detection and investigation of such modifications.
rules.target: Success and Failure, Failure, Failure, Success and Failure

rules.title: System integrity auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records events that affect the integrity of the security subsystem, including changes to audit policy and related integrity-relevant actions.
rules.impact: System integrity audit events support detection of unauthorized audit policy changes and provide evidence needed during security incident investigation.

rules.title: Lock screen camera disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the camera can be used while the lock screen is displayed.
rules.impact: A camera available on the lock screen may allow unauthorized image or video capture without an authenticated session.

rules.title: Lock screen slideshow disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether a slideshow of images can run on the lock screen.
rules.impact: Slideshow content may expose sensitive images left in the slideshow folder to anyone with physical access to the console before sign-in.

rules.title: LAPS password expiration protection enabled
rules.explanation: When Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) is used, this policy enforces Password Settings Object (PSO) age limits so the managed local administrator password cannot be reset to a longer lifetime. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: LAPS provides unique, periodically rotated passwords for local administrator accounts on domain-joined systems. Without expiration protection, password age can be extended, increasing the window for credential reuse and compromise.

rules.title: LAPS local administrator password management enabled
rules.explanation: This setting enables LAPS management of the local administrator password on domain-joined systems. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Without LAPS, local administrator passwords are often shared or rarely rotated, increasing the risk that a single compromised credential can be reused across many systems.

rules.title: LAPS password complexity configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the password complexity requirements applied by LAPS to the managed local administrator account. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Weak local administrator passwords increase the likelihood of brute-force or password-guessing attacks against privileged local accounts.

rules.title: LAPS password age configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the maximum age, in days, of the LAPS-managed local administrator password before it is rotated. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Infrequent password rotation lengthens the useful life of a stolen local administrator credential and increases lateral-movement risk.

rules.title: Automatic administrator logon disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows automatically signs in with a stored administrator account at startup (AutoAdminLogon).
rules.impact: Automatic logon grants console access without credentials and stores the account password in the registry in clear text, exposing the system to anyone with physical or local registry access.

rules.title: IPv4 source routing protection level configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures how the system handles IPv4 packets that use IP source routing.
rules.impact: Permissive source routing can assist IP spoofing and traffic-redirection attacks by allowing packets to specify their own path through the network.

rules.title: ICMP redirects disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the system accepts ICMP redirect messages that can alter existing IP routes.
rules.impact: Accepting ICMP redirects allows an attacker to manipulate routing so traffic is diverted to an unintended host, enabling interception or follow-on attacks.

rules.title: TCP keep-alive time configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines how often TCP keep-alive packets are sent to verify that an idle connection is still valid.
rules.impact: An unbounded or poorly chosen keep-alive interval can be abused to maintain or amplify connection load and contribute to denial-of-service conditions.

rules.title: NetBIOS name-release requests ignored except from WINS
rules.explanation: This setting configures NetBIOS over TCP/IP to ignore name-release requests that do not originate from WINS servers (NoNameReleaseOnDemand).
rules.impact: Honoring unsolicited NetBIOS name-release requests can allow an attacker to force name conflicts, enabling NetBIOS name spoofing and denial-of-service against name resolution.

rules.title: IRDP router discovery disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the system performs ICMP Router Discovery Protocol (IRDP) to locate routers on the local network.
rules.impact: With IRDP enabled, a compromised host on the subnet can advertise itself as a router and cause other systems to forward traffic through it.

rules.title: Safe DLL search mode enabled
rules.explanation: Safe DLL Search Mode changes the order in which Windows searches for DLLs so that system directories are preferred over the current working directory.
rules.impact: Without Safe DLL Search Mode, applications may load a malicious DLL placed in a writable directory ahead of the legitimate system library, enabling code execution.

rules.title: Screen saver grace period configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the delay, in seconds, between screen saver activation and the workstation becoming locked.
rules.impact: An excessive grace period leaves an unlocked interactive session available after the screen saver starts, increasing the risk of unauthorized console access.

rules.title: TCP maximum data retransmissions configured
rules.explanation: This setting limits how many times unacknowledged TCP data segments are retransmitted before the connection is abandoned.
rules.impact: Unlimited or excessive retransmissions can be leveraged to prolong resource consumption and contribute to denial-of-service against TCP services.

rules.title: Security event log warning level configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the percentage of Security event log capacity at which a warning is generated that the log is approaching capacity.
rules.impact: Without timely capacity warnings, the Security log may fill and stop recording new events, reducing visibility for incident detection and investigation.

rules.title: LLMNR multicast name resolution disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR), which resolves names on the local subnet using multicast queries.
rules.impact: LLMNR can be abused with malicious multicast responses to redirect name resolution and facilitate credential capture or man-in-the-middle attacks.

rules.title: Third-party font providers disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows can download and use fonts from third-party font providers.
rules.impact: Third-party font providers introduce unapproved content and network calls that expand the attack surface and can conflict with enterprise change-control requirements.

rules.title: Insecure guest logons to SMB shares disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the SMB client may use insecure guest authentication when connecting to file shares.
rules.impact: Insecure guest logons allow unauthenticated access to shared resources and can expose sensitive data without accountability.

rules.title: LLTDIO mapper I/O disabled on domain networks
rules.explanation: This setting controls the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Mapper I/O (LLTDIO) driver on domain-joined networks used for network map discovery.
rules.impact: Network topology discovery can expose the host to unauthorized or attacker-controlled devices that participate in topology mapping.

rules.title: LLTD Responder (RSPNDR) disabled on domain networks
rules.explanation: This setting controls the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Responder (RSPNDR) driver on domain-joined networks.
rules.impact: Responding to topology discovery requests can expose the host to unauthorized devices and assist mapping of the internal network.

rules.title: Peer-to-peer networking disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables Microsoft Peer-to-Peer Networking (Peernet) on the system.
rules.impact: Peer-to-peer networking creates ad hoc connectivity paths that are difficult to control and can be abused for unauthorized data transfer or lateral communication.

rules.title: Network bridge creation disabled on domain networks
rules.explanation: This setting prevents users from creating or modifying a network bridge when Network Location Awareness identifies a domain network.
rules.impact: A network bridge can join otherwise separate networks and allow unintended traffic flow between them, which an attacker can abuse for pivoting or data exfiltration.

rules.title: Internet Connection Sharing UI disabled
rules.explanation: This setting removes the user interface for enabling Internet Connection Sharing (ICS) as an Internet gateway.
rules.impact: ICS can turn a workstation into an uncontrolled Internet gateway, bypassing perimeter controls and allowing unmanaged outbound access.

rules.title: Standard domain users prohibited from setting network location
rules.explanation: This setting requires elevation when a standard domain user attempts to change the network location (for example, when mapping or classifying a network connection).
rules.impact: Allowing standard users to set network location increases the attack surface by permitting changes that can weaken firewall profiles or network trust boundaries.

rules.title: Windows Connect Now registrars disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables Windows Connect Now (WCN) registrar functionality used for simplified wireless configuration and credential transfer.
rules.impact: WCN simplifies wireless provisioning and can be abused to propagate network credentials or configurations to unauthorized devices.

rules.title: Simultaneous Internet or domain connections minimized
rules.explanation: This Windows Connection Manager policy limits how computers establish multiple simultaneous connections to the Internet or a Windows domain.
rules.impact: Multiple concurrent connections can create uncontrolled paths to external networks and complicate enforcement of corporate connectivity policy.

rules.title: Simultaneous domain and non-domain connections blocked
rules.explanation: This setting determines whether a system may connect to a domain network and a non-domain network at the same time.
rules.impact: Concurrent domain and public network connections increase the risk that corporate traffic is exposed or routed through less trusted networks.

rules.title: UAC token filtering for remote local accounts enabled
rules.explanation: LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy controls whether remote network logons using local accounts receive a full elevated token or a filtered UAC token.
rules.impact: Local account credentials are frequently targeted. Applying UAC filtering to remote local-account logons reduces the privileges available to an attacker using stolen local credentials over the network.

rules.title: WDigest credential caching disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether WDigest authentication stores a reusable copy of the user's clear-text password in memory (UseLogonCredential).
rules.impact: When WDigest caching is enabled, clear-text credentials in LSASS memory can be recovered by an attacker with local privileged access.

rules.title: Process creation command-line auditing excluded
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether command-line arguments are included in process creation audit events.
rules.impact: Including command-line details in audit events can expose secrets such as passwords or tokens to anyone who can read the Security log.

rules.title: Early Launch Anti-Malware driver load policy configured
rules.explanation: This Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) policy defines which boot-start drivers are allowed to initialize based on the ELAM driver's classification.
rules.impact: Without a restrictive driver load policy, untrusted boot-start drivers may load before antimalware protection is active and execute malicious code at boot.

rules.title: Background Group Policy processing enabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Group Policy is refreshed in the background without requiring a reboot or user re-logon.
rules.impact: Without background refresh, systems may continue operating under outdated security settings until the next restart or interactive logon.

rules.title: Group Policy processing forced even when GPOs are unchanged
rules.explanation: This setting forces Group Policy to reapply domain policy even when the GPO list has not changed since the last refresh.
rules.impact: Forcing policy reapplication helps restore intended domain security settings after unauthorized local changes.

rules.title: Cross-device experience (CDP) disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the device may participate in cross-device experiences that share activity and connectivity with other user devices (Continue experiences / CDP).
rules.impact: Cross-device communication expands trust relationships beyond the managed host and introduces additional paths for data exposure or abuse.

rules.title: HTTP-based print driver downloads disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether print drivers can be downloaded over HTTP (Web PnP download).
rules.impact: Downloading drivers over HTTP lacks transport integrity guarantees and may allow users to obtain tampered drivers that contain malicious code.

rules.title: Handwriting recognition error reports disabled
rules.explanation: This setting prevents the handwriting recognition error reporting tool from sending handwriting samples or related reports.
rules.impact: Handwriting samples can constitute personally identifiable information, including signatures, and automatic upload may violate privacy or data-handling policy.

rules.title: Internet Connection Wizard Microsoft ISP download disabled
rules.explanation: This setting configures the Internet Connection Wizard to exit rather than contact Microsoft to download an ISP list (ExitOnMSICW).
rules.impact: Unneeded outbound connections to retrieve ISP listings increase exposure and are typically unnecessary in managed enterprise environments.

rules.title: Online Windows Registration Wizard disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows Registration Wizard so users cannot complete online product registration interactively.
rules.impact: In enterprise environments, individual online registration of Windows copies can create uncontrolled outbound connections and inconsistent asset registration.

rules.title: Search Companion content file updates disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables automatic download of content file updates used by Search Companion for local and Internet search.
